title: Threat Vectors and Sources

header.html: the official CompTIA Security+ SY0-801 V8 exam objectives, document version 2.0

toc.title: Supply chain, media and human vectors

html:
1Vectors and the attack surface

A threat vector is a path an attacker uses to reach a target. The attack surface is all the places an attacker could try. A smaller surface means less risk.

A related term from the objectives is the advanced persistent threat (APT): a skilled, patient attacker, often state-backed, who stays hidden in a network for a long time.

2Message-based and content-based vectors

Vector Details
Message-based Email, SMS, RCS (Rich Communication Services), instant messaging, collaboration tools: used for phishing, smishing and malicious links
Image-based QR codes (quishing), embedded content, and CAPTCHA images abused to trick users
Attachment-based Embedded macros in documents, RTF documents, PDFs with malicious code or links
Browser-based Extensions, JavaScript, password managers, cookies and session tokens that can be stolen
Exam tip

. A QR code that sends a victim to a fake site is image-based (quishing). Macros in an Office file are attachment-based. A stolen session token lets an attacker skip the password.

3Network, remote and endpoint vectors

Vector Details
Network-based Infrastructure devices (switches, routers), virtualized devices, stolen session keys
Remote access Remote desktop (RDP), VNC, VPN: exposed or weakly protected entry points
Endpoint-based Mobile devices, workstations, servers, tablets, trusted devices, built-in tools and living-off-the-land tools (legitimate system tools that attackers abuse)
IoT-based Cameras, sensors, printers: often weak or default passwords and no patching
OT-based Operational technology such as industrial control systems: long life, hard to patch
Exam tip

. Living off the land means attackers use tools already on the system (PowerShell, scripts) to avoid detection. An exposed remote desktop with a weak password is a classic remote access vector.

4Supply chain, media and human vectors

Vector Details
Supply chain-based Third-party providers, managed service providers (MSPs), logistics providers, SaaS providers: a compromised supplier reaches many customers
External media-based A malicious USB drive left or handed to a victim
Human-based Impersonation, contractor, visitor, biometric spoofing, watering hole (compromising a site the targets visit)
Physical-based Lock and key, access vestibule (a double-door entry), access passes
Signal-based Bluetooth, radio frequency (RF), near-field communications (NFC)

Exam tip

. A watering hole attack compromises a website the target group visits. A compromise of a managed service provider that reaches all its customers is a supply chain attack. An access vestibule helps stop tailgating (physical).

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors finds that a poster with a QR code led visitors to a fake sign-in page. Which vector is this?

  • AAttachment-based
  • BImage-based
  • CSupply chain-based
  • DRemote access
Show the answer

Answer: B. A malicious QR code is an image-based vector, often called quishing.

S2Attackers compromise a software vendor's update server and push malware to all of the vendor's customers. Which vector is this?

  • AWatering hole
  • BSupply chain
  • CRemovable media
  • DSignal-based
Show the answer

Answer: B. A compromised supplier delivering malicious updates to many customers is a supply chain attack.

S3A user plugs in a USB drive found in the parking lot and malware runs. Which vector is this?

  • AExternal media-based
  • BBrowser-based
  • CMessage-based
  • DNetwork-based
Show the answer

Answer: A. A malicious USB device is an external media-based vector.

S4Attackers use PowerShell already installed on a workstation to move through the network without dropping new files. What is this technique called?

  • ALiving off the land
  • BTailgating
  • CWatering hole
  • DPretexting
Show the answer

Answer: A. Using legitimate built-in tools to avoid detection is living off the land.

S5An attacker infects a trade association's website that the target engineers visit daily. Which attack is this?

  • AWatering hole
  • BSmishing
  • CVishing
  • DShoulder surfing
Show the answer

Answer: A. Compromising a site that the target group often visits is a watering hole attack.

S6A building adds a double-door entry where only one person can pass at a time after badge validation. Which risk does it reduce the most?

  • APhishing
  • BTailgating
  • CCookie theft
  • DDNS poisoning
Show the answer

Answer: B. An access vestibule prevents unauthorized people from following an authorized person inside.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What is a threat vector?

Show the answer

A path an attacker uses to reach a target.

R2What does RCS stand for, and which vector is it?

Show the answer

Rich Communication Services; a message-based vector.

R3Which browser items can be abused?

Show the answer

Extensions, JavaScript, password managers, cookies and session tokens.

R4Name three IoT devices named in the objectives.

Show the answer

Cameras, sensors and printers.

R5What is a watering hole attack?

Show the answer

Compromising a site that the target group visits.

R6Name three signal-based vectors.

Show the answer

Bluetooth, radio frequency and near-field communications.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Message and content email, SMS, RCS, IM, collaboration; QR codes, embedded content, CAPTCHA; macros, RTF, PDF; browser extensions, JavaScript, cookies, session tokens
Network and endpoint infrastructure devices, remote access (RDP, VNC, VPN); mobile, workstations, servers, living-off-the-land tools; IoT and OT
Supply chain and people third parties, MSPs, logistics, SaaS; malicious USB; impersonation, contractor, visitor, watering hole
Physical and signal lock and key, access vestibule, passes; Bluetooth, RF, NFC
